test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A vendor sold 25 laptops at a profit of 12% and 15 laptops at a profit of 20%. If he had sold all the 40 laptops at a profit of 18%, his profit would have increased by Rs. 30,000. What is the cost price of each laptop, if the cost price of all the 40 laptops is the same?
solution:
**Given:**

Profit percentage of 25 laptops = 12%

Profit percentage of 15 laptops = 20%

Profit percentage of all the 40 laptops = 18%

Increase in profit = Rs. 30000

**Formula used:**

Profit\: \%={Profitover CP}×100 

**Calculations:**

Let the cost price of 1 laptop = Rs. x

The cost price of 25 laptop = Rs. 25x

The cost price of 15 laptop = Rs. 15x

The cost price of 40 laptop = Rs. 40x

Now, profit can be calculated as,

For 25 laptops,

​ Profit\: \%={Profitover CP}×100\ 12={Profitover 25x}×100\ Profit={12times 25xover 100}\ Profit=3x 

 
• For 15 laptops,

 Profit\: \%={Profitover CP}×100\ 20={Profitover 15x}×100\ Profit={20times 15xover 100}\ Profit=3x 

 
• For 40 laptops,

 Profit\: \%={Profitover CP}×100\ 18={Profitover 40x}×100\ Profit={18times 40xover 100}\ Profit=7.2x 

According to the question,

Profit of 40 laptops+30000 = Profit of 25 laptops + Profit of 15 laptops

 7.2x+30000=3x+3x\ 7.2x-6x=30000\ 1.2x=30000\ x=25000

Hence, **the cost price of each laptop is Rs. 25000.**
